description: Error fingerprinting and deduplication for ErrorHistory (docs/features/error-history.md#error-fingerprinting). Fingerprint = lowercase hex SHA-256(error_code + ':' + module_id + ':' + normalize_message(message)), UTF-8. normalize_message replaces, in this order, UUIDs with <UUID>, ISO 8601 dates and timestamps with <TIMESTAMP> and integers of four or more digits with <ID>, then trims and lowercases. The call site is not an input: stack frames differ between Python, V8 and Rust, so including one would give the same error a different fingerprint in each SDK. Two errors with the same fingerprint MUST collapse into a single ErrorEntry (count incremented, last_seen_at updated). Different error_code values, or different module_id values, MUST produce distinct fingerprints.

driver_contract.module_id: Each error's `caller_id` is the `module_id` argument of ErrorHistory.record — the module whose call failed, which is what the error-history middleware passes. No other value (a stack frame, a caller) is part of the fingerprint.

errors.message: Connection timed out for request a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
Connection timed out for request ffffffff-eeee-dddd-cccc-bbbbbbbbbbbb
Rate limit exceeded at 2026-05-03T10:15:30Z, retry after 30s
Rate limit exceeded at 2026-05-03T11:20:45Z, retry after 30s

expected._note: shard 42 (2 digits) is preserved; 123456/987654 (>=4 digits) collapse to <ID>
Identical message after normalization, but different error_code MUST yield distinct fingerprints
Same code and same normalized message in two different modules MUST yield distinct fingerprints: module_id is part of the fingerprint.

test_cases.description: D-120: every timestamp ErrorHistory writes is `2026-09-16T10:30:00.123Z` — exactly three fractional digits and a `Z` suffix. Measured before the decision: `+00:00` microseconds in apcore-python, `Z` milliseconds in apcore-typescript, `Z` microseconds in apcore-rust, and apcore-rust's health summary reformatted the same record with `to_rfc3339()` into a third form. Asserting the suffix alone would leave three precisions behind one `Z`: the same divergence, harder to see. All three timestamp fields are checked, because a fix applied to one of them is the divergence again at one field's remove.
